audit.title: Evidence-Based Security & Database Integrity Sign-Off
audit.auditor: Principal Engineer, PostgreSQL Security Auditor & Technical Co-Founder
audit.target_environment: Isolated Disposable PostgreSQL 16 (Docker: mcqj-postgres-test on 127.0.0.1:5433, tmpfs 1GB)
audit.status: AUDIT COMPLETE — ALL CRITICAL & HIGH FINDINGS FIXED & VERIFIED

findings.title: Gate 0 Caller Role Confusion in SECURITY DEFINER Stored Procedures
findings.evidence: In PostgreSQL, CURRENT_USER inside a SECURITY DEFINER function evaluates to the function owner ('postgres'), not the invoking role. In prior code, 'ELSIF CURRENT_USER IN ('postgres', 'service_role')' was evaluated when auth.uid() was NULL. Because CURRENT_USER was always 'postgres', any unauthenticated web request or PostgREST call without a JWT entered Case 2 ('Trusted Backend Execution') and accepted 'p_admin_user_id' as verified caller identity, permitting unauthorized publication or re-evaluation.
findings.exploitability_impact: Critical. Allowed any caller capable of invoking the function without a JWT to supply an arbitrary administrator UUID in p_admin_user_id and execute administrative publication or attempt re-evaluation.
findings.before_behavior: ELSIF CURRENT_USER IN ('postgres', 'service_role') evaluated true for unauthenticated callers, trusting p_admin_user_id parameter blindly.
findings.after_behavior: Added Guard 0.1 immediately rejecting auth.role() = 'anon'; Guard 0.3 rejecting authenticated web sessions missing auth.uid(); and Guard 0.4 requiring SESSION_USER IN ('postgres', 'service_role') AND auth.role() IS NULL for direct backend execution. Untrusted or unauthenticated calls fail closed.
findings.remediation: Updated migration.sql Gate 0 in both fn_publish_exam_paper and fn_reevaluate_paper_attempts to use SESSION_USER, auth.role(), and explicit fail-closed boundaries.

findings.title: Alternate Write Paths Bypassing Booklet Option Mapping Occurrence Alignment
findings.evidence: While trg_booklet_option_mapping_integrity prevented inserting or updating booklet_option_mappings directly with cross-question options, parent records in unverified/draft papers could be updated: modifying booklet_question_mappings.occurrence_id or reparenting question_options.representation_id would leave existing booklet_option_mappings pointing to mismatched occurrences.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Could lead to exam booklet desynchronization where displayed options do not correspond to the question occurrence, corrupting student exam attempts.
findings.before_behavior: Updating parent occurrence_id on booklet_question_mappings or representation_id on question_options did not check existing child option mappings.
findings.after_behavior: Added trg_booklet_qmap_occurrence_guard raising MCQJ-ERR-4008 if occurrence_id is altered while option mappings exist. Added trg_question_option_rep_guard raising MCQJ-ERR-4009 if representation_id is reparented across occurrences while option mappings exist.
findings.remediation: Implemented parent mutation triggers in migration.sql and added NULL validation checks to fn_guard_booklet_option_mapping_integrity.

findings.title: Plaintext Test Database Credentials in Test Harness Output & Documentation
findings.evidence: The local disposable Docker test password (<REDACTED_LOCAL_TEST_SECRET>) was printed in plaintext in test harness fatal error examples and committed report artifacts.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. While the credential was local-only and not present in .env.local, hardcoding credentials in reports sets a dangerous precedent and violates credential-hygiene standards.
findings.before_behavior: Plaintext password displayed in error messages and report tables.
findings.after_behavior: Mandated TEST_DB_PASSWORD environment variable with fail-closed behavior; redacted passwords in test harness error output to <REDACTED_PASSWORD>; redacted all plaintext secrets in audit reports.
findings.remediation: Replaced hardcoded strings with redacted placeholders and parameterized Docker compose service.

findings.title: PostgREST Defense-in-Depth for Anonymous Role Privilege Bounds
findings.evidence: REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon prevented PostgREST from calling procedures, but function bodies did not explicitly check auth.role() = 'anon' as an internal defense-in-depth gate in the event of database privilege grants misconfiguration.
findings.exploitability_impact: Informational / Defense-in-Depth. If an administrator accidentally granted execute to anon or PUBLIC in the future, anonymous callers could attempt invocation.
findings.before_behavior: Function relied solely on SQL grant revocation to block anon callers.
findings.after_behavior: Function body enforces Guard 0.1 explicitly checking auth.role() = 'anon' and raising MCQJ-ERR-5015 before any processing.
findings.remediation: Added Guard 0.1 inside stored procedures in migration.sql.
